en: A Brief Exposition of the Dharma-Gate for the Cultivation and Realization of the Sacred Stages as Distinguished in the Yoga of the Vajraśekhara,
by [the one holding the rank of] Kai-fu-yi-tong-san-si, Te-jin, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Duke of Su.

The Imperially Enfeoffed Lord of Three Thousand Households, conferred the rank of Grand Master of Works (Sikong) and the purple robe, posthumously titled Dajian (Great Mirror), bearing the honorific title Da Guangzhi (Great Universal Wisdom), the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery, translated this by imperial decree. At that time, the Vairocana Buddha of the Vajradhātu, residing in the Akaniṣṭha Heaven Palace at the summit of the Realm of Form, initially attained equal and perfect enlightenment as the Saṃbhogakāya. He realized the equalizing wisdom of all Tathāgatas and immediately entered the Samaya of the Vajra Equalizing Wisdom-Seal of all Tathāgatas, thereby realizing the Treasury of Wisdom of the Radiant Self-Nature of the Dharma-Equality of all Tathāgatas.

Having attained perfect enlightenment, all the Tathāgatas emerged from the Sattvavajra as the Great Maṇi Jewel of the Gaganagañja, and they consecrated his crown, causing the wisdom of the Dharma King Avalokiteśvara to arise within him and establishing the skillful wisdom of Viśvakarman of all the Tathāgatas, thereby sending him to the Vajramaṇiratna-śikhara-kūṭāgāra at the summit of Mount Sumeru.
Once the assembly of noble ones had gathered, Vairocana Buddha empowered all the Tathāgatas and prepared lion thrones for them to sit upon in the four directions.
At that time, Akṣobhya Tathāgata, Ratnasambhava Tathāgata, Avalokiteśvararāja Tathāgata, and Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata, in turn, empowered Vairocana Buddha.
However, there are two types of enjoyment bodies (*saṃbhogakāya*):
first, the self-enjoyment body; second, the other-enjoyment body.
Vairocana Buddha internally realizes the four wisdoms of self-enjoyment within his own mind.

The Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom, the Wisdom of Equality, the Wisdom of Wondrous Observation, and the Wisdom of Accomplishing What is to be Done externally cause the ten stages to be fulfilled for the sake of the "other-enjoyment" of Bodhisattvas; thus, from within these four wisdoms, the four Buddhas flow forth, each abiding in their respective directions and seated upon their respective thrones.

Vairocana Buddha realizes within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the five-crested vajra bodhicitta; for the sake of self-enjoyment, from this samādhi-wisdom of the five-crested vajra bodhicitta, he emits vajra light that illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, purifying the great bodhicitta of all sentient beings.

It returns and merges into one body, and in order to provide enjoyment for all bodhisattvas through this samādhi-wisdom, it takes the form of the Vajra-pāramitā and dwells upon the moon disc before the Tathāgata Vairocana.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the Great Maṇi Jewel of Space-Treasury, for the sake of his own enjoyment, causes the light of the space-treasury jewel to flow forth from that samādhi-wisdom of the Great Maṇi Jewel of Space-Treasury. This light shines universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions, causing the merit of all sentient beings to become perfected.

It then returns and merges into a single body; for the sake of allowing all bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, it takes the form of the Vajra-Jewel Pāramitā and dwells upon the moon disc to the right of the Tathāgata Vairocana.

Vairocana Buddha realizes within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Great Vajra-Exertion of Karma; because it is for his own enjoyment, from this samādhi-wisdom of the Great Vajra-Exertion of Karma he emits the light of Karma, which shines throughout the worlds of the ten directions, causing all sentient beings to eliminate all indolence and achieve great exertion.

It returns and merges into one body; then, so that all bodhisattvas may enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, it takes the form of the Karma-pāramitā and dwells upon the moon disc to the left of the Tathāgata Vairocana.

Vairocana Buddha realizes within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Great Lotus; for the sake of his own enjoyment, from this samādhi-wisdom of the Great Lotus he emits lotus-light that pervasively illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, purifying all adventitious afflictions of sentient beings.

It then returns and merges into one body; in order to provide the samādhi-wisdom for the enjoyment of all Bodhisattvas, it takes the form of the Dharma-pāramitā and dwells upon the moon-disc behind the Tathāgata Vairocana.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the courageous bodhicitta of Vajrasattva for his own enjoyment, emitted from that samādhi-wisdom of the courageous bodhicitta of Vajrasattva five-peaked vajra light that pervaded the worlds of the ten directions, causing all sentient beings to suddenly realize the conduct of Samantabhadra;

it then returned and merged into one body, and for the sake of enabling all Bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, he took the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva and dwelt upon the moon disc before Akṣobhya Tathāgata.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the four means of attraction (saṃgrahavastu) as the vajra-hook, for the sake of his own enjoyment, emits vajra-light from the samādhi-wisdom of the vajra-hook and the four means of attraction. This light shines universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions, gathering all sentient beings through the four means of attraction and establishing them in unsurpassed bodhi.

It then returns and merges into one body; in order to provide the samādhi-wisdom for the enjoyment of all Bodhisattvas, he manifests in the form of Vajrarāja Bodhisattva and dwells upon the moon-disc to the right of Akṣobhya Tathāgata.

Vairocana Buddha, having realized within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Affection Great Compassion Arrow, for the sake of his own enjoyment, emits from that samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Affection Great Compassion Arrow rays of vajra-arrows that illuminate the worlds of the ten directions. These rays strike and subdue those among all sentient beings who harbor feelings of aversion toward unsurpassed bodhi.

They then return and merge into a single essence; in order to allow all bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, he takes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajra-Affection and dwells upon the moon disc to the left of Akṣobhya Tathāgata.

Vairocana Buddha, having realized within his own mind the *samādhi* and wisdom of the Vajra-Excellent-Joyful-Wrathful-King (*vajrasādhu-saumanasya-vikrīḍita-rāja*), for the sake of his own enjoyment, emits from the wisdom of the *vajrasādhu-saumanasya-vikrīḍita-samādhi* the light of the *vajrasādhu-mudrā*, which illuminates the worlds of the ten directions. It shines upon all sentient beings who feel dejection regarding the conduct of Samantabhadra and harbor inferior intentions, causing them to attain a body and mind through the wisdom of joyful writhing (*vikrīḍita*).

Returning and merging back into a single essence, in order to provide the enjoyment of *samādhi*-wisdom for all Bodhisattvas, he takes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrasādhu and dwells upon the moon disc behind the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.

Vairocana Buddha realizes within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Jewel Initiation; for his own enjoyment, from this samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Jewel Initiation, he emits vajra-jewel light that illuminates the worlds of the ten directions and sprinkles upon the crowns of the heads of all sentient beings, causing them to attain the stage of non-retrogression as Bodhisattvas.

Returning to merge into one body, in order to provide all Bodhisattvas with the enjoyment of samādhi-wisdom, he takes the form of the Vajra-Jewel Bodhisattva and dwells before the moon disc in front of Ratnasambhava Tathāgata.

Vairocana Buddha realizes the wisdom of the *vajratejorāśi-samādhi* within his own mind; for the sake of self-enjoyment, from this wisdom of the *vajratejorāśi-samādhi*, he emits the radiance of the vajra-sun, which illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, shatters the ignorance and darkness of all sentient beings, and gives rise to the light of great wisdom.

This light returns and merges into a single essence; then, so that all bodhisattvas may enjoy the wisdom of samādhi, he manifests in the form of the Bodhisattva Vajratejas and dwells upon the lunar disc to the right of Ratnasambhava Tathāgata.

Vairocana Buddha realizes within his own mind the wisdom of the *vajraratnaketu-samādhi*; for the sake of his own enjoyment (*svasaṃbhoga*), he emits from the wisdom of the *vajraratnaketu-samādhi* the light of the Vajra Banner, which illuminates the worlds of the ten directions and fulfills the aspirations of all sentient beings.

This light returns and merges into one body; then, in order to allow all Bodhisattvas to enjoy the wisdom of samādhi, he manifests in the form of the Bodhisattva Vajraketu and dwells upon the moon disc to the left of Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Laughter-Seal Prophecy (*vajrahāsamudrāvyākaraṇasamādhi-jñāna*), because it is for his own enjoyment (*svasaṃbhoga*), emits from the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Laughter-Seal Prophecy the light of the Vajra-Laughter-Seal. This light shines universally upon sentient beings of indeterminate nature throughout the worlds of the ten directions, bestowing upon them the prophecy of equal, unsurpassed bodhi.

It then returns and merges into one body; in order to allow all Bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, he takes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrahāsa and dwells within the moon disc behind the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the vajra-dharma’s purity and non-defilement for his own enjoyment, emits from that samādhi-wisdom of the vajra-dharma’s purity and non-defilement the radiance of the vajra-dharma, which illuminates the worlds of the ten directions. It purifies the bodies and minds of all sentient beings’ five desires, making them as pure as lotuses unsullied by dust or grime.

Returning, it reabsorbs into a single essence; then, so that all bodhisattvas may enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, it takes the form of the Vajradharma Bodhisattva and dwells within the moon disc before the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja.

Vairocana Buddha realized within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Sharp Sword Prajñāpāramitā; for his own enjoyment, from that samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Sharp Sword Pāramitā, he emitted the radiance of the Vajra-Sharp Sword, which illuminated the worlds of the ten directions, severing the fetters of all sentient beings and freeing them from all suffering and affliction.

It then returned and merged into a single essence. In order to provide the samādhi-wisdom for the enjoyment of all Bodhisattvas, it took the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrakhadga and dwelt upon the moon disc to the right of the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja.

Vairocana Buddha, having realized within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Cause Wheel-Turning, for the sake of his own enjoyment, emitted from that samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Cause Wheel-Turning rays of light in the form of vajra-wheels. These illuminated the worlds of the ten directions, gathering all sentient beings through the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) and establishing them in unsurpassed bodhi.

Returning and reabsorbing into a single body, in order to provide the samādhi-wisdom for the enjoyment of all bodhisattvas, he manifested in the form of the Bodhisattva Vajra-Cause and dwelt upon the moon disc to the left of the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja.

Vairocana Buddha, within his own mind, realized the samādhi-wisdom of the adamantine secret speech that transcends verbal expression. For his own enjoyment, from this samādhi-wisdom of the adamantine secret speech that transcends verbal expression, he emitted the light of the adamantine tongue-mark, which illuminated the worlds of the ten directions and was able to eliminate the evil wisdom of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, causing them to attain the four kinds of unimpeded analytical knowledge (*pratisaṃvid*) and the eloquence of joyful exposition (*pratibhāna*).

This light then returned and merged into one body; for the sake of allowing all bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, it manifested in the form of the Bodhisattva Vajravāc and dwelt upon the moon disc behind the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja.

Vairocana Buddha realizes within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-karma Ākāśa-kośa (Vajra-Action Space-Treasury). For his own enjoyment, he emits from the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-karma Ākāśa-kośa the light of vajra-action, which illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, causing all sentient beings to perform vast offerings to all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.

Returning and reabsorbing into a single essence, in order to provide enjoyment for all Bodhisattvas through this samādhi-wisdom, he takes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrakarma and dwells upon the moon disc in front of the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Protecting Great Compassion Adorned Armor, for the sake of his own enjoyment, emitted from the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Protecting Great Compassion Adorned Armor the light of the Vajra Armor. This light pervaded the worlds of the ten directions, able to eliminate the violent, evil, and wrathful sentient beings so that they might swiftly attain a mind of great compassion;
it then returned and merged into one body.
In order to allow all bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, he manifested in the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāla and dwelt upon the moon disc to the right of the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the wisdom of the *vajrayakṣa-upāya-bhīṣaṇa-samādhi* for his own enjoyment, emits from that wisdom of the *vajrayakṣa-upāya-bhīṣaṇa-samādhi* light rays of vajra-fangs that illuminate the worlds of the ten directions. He subdues sentient beings who are stubborn and difficult to transform, establishing them on the path to enlightenment;

then, returning to merge into one body, in order to allow all bodhisattvas to enjoy the wisdom of *samādhi*, he takes the form of the Vajrayakṣa Bodhisattva and dwells upon the moon disc to the left of the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the majestic and responsive Vajra-fist mudrā for his own enjoyment, emanates from that samādhi-wisdom of the majestic and responsive Vajra-fist a light of the Vajra-fist that illuminates the worlds of the ten directions. This causes all sentient beings to eliminate their karmic obstructions and swiftly attain the perfection of both mundane and supramundane siddhis;
the light then returns and merges back into one with him.
In order to cause all bodhisattvas to partake in the wisdom of samādhi, he assumes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi and dwells upon the moon disc at the rear of the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi.

Vairocana Buddha, within his own mind, realizes the samādhi-wisdom of the insignia of the Vajra-playful Dharma-bliss (*vajralāsyā-dharmasukha-lakṣaṇa-samādhi-jñāna*). For the sake of his own enjoyment, from this samādhi-wisdom of the insignia of the Vajra-playful Dharma-bliss, he emits the light of the insignia of the Vajra-playful [goddess], which illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, makes offerings to all Tathāgatas, and destroys the worldly pleasures of the defiled greed of ordinary beings, causing them to attain the bliss of the garden of playful Dharma.

This light returns and reabsorbs into a single essence; then, for the sake of enabling all Bodhisattvas to enjoy the samādhi-wisdom, he manifests as the Bodhisattva in the form of the goddess Vajralāsyā and dwells upon the moon disc in the southeast corner of Vairocana Tathāgata.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the bodhipakṣa-dharma of the Vajra Flower Garland (*vajrapuṣpamālā*), for the sake of his own enjoyment, emits from the samādhi-wisdom of the bodhipakṣa-dharma of the Vajra Flower Garland a light of the Vajra Flower Garland that illuminates the worlds of the ten directions and makes offerings to all Tathāgatas. This light removes the ugly forms of all sentient beings, causing them to obtain bodies endowed with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics.

Returning and merging back into one body, in order to provide the samādhi-wisdom for the enjoyment of all Bodhisattvas, he manifests as the Bodhisattva in the form of the goddess Vajrapuṣpamālā and dwells upon the moon disc in the southwest corner of Vairocana Buddha.

Vairocana Buddha realizes within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the pure and wondrous Dharma-sound of Vajra Chanting. For his own enjoyment, from the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra Chanting Pure Dharma-Wheel, he emits the light of Vajra Chanting, which illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, makes offerings to all Tathāgatas, and enables sentient beings to destroy the conceptual proliferation of verbal karma and attain the endowment of the sixty-four kinds of Brahma-voices.

Returning and merging into one body, for the sake of enabling all Bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, he manifests as the Bodhisattva in the form of the Vajra Chanting Goddess and dwells upon the moon-disc in the northwest corner of Vairocana Buddha.

Vairocana Buddha realized within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the miraculous play of the Vajra-Dharma Dance. For his own enjoyment, from that samādhi-wisdom of the miraculous play of the Vajra-Dharma Dance, he emitted the light of the Vajra Dance, which illuminated the worlds of the ten directions, made offerings to all Tathāgatas, and shattered the ignorance and nescience of all sentient beings, whereby they attained the sovereign play of the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*).

This light returned and merged back into one body; then, so that all Bodhisattvas might enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, he manifested as the Bodhisattva in the form of the goddess Vajra-Dharma-Nartī, and dwelt upon the moon disc in the northeast corner of Vairocana Buddha.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra Incense Cloud-Ocean, for the sake of his own enjoyment, emanates vajra incense from that samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra Incense Cloud-Ocean. Its light shines universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions, making offerings to all Tathāgatas and destroying the foul-smelling afflictions of all sentient beings, whereby they obtain the fragrance of unimpeded wisdom that brings joy.

It then returns and merges into one body; in order to allow all Bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, it takes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajra Incense Maid and dwells in the southeast corner of the Vajra Jewel Pavilion.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Awakening-Flower-Cloud-Ocean, for the sake of his own enjoyment, emits from the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Awakening-Flower-Cloud-Ocean the radiance of the Vajra-Awakening-Flower. This light pervasively illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, making offerings to all Tathāgatas, dispelling the delusions of all sentient beings, causing the flowers of their minds to bloom, and leading them to realize untainted wisdom.

It then returns and merges into one body; in order to allow all Bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, it takes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajra-Awakening-Flower Attendant and dwells in the Vajra-Jewel Pavilion at the southwest corner.

Vairocana Buddha realizes within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra Lamp-Light Cloud-Ocean; for the sake of his own enjoyment, from this samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra Lamp-Light Cloud-Ocean, he emits the radiance of the Vajra Lamp-Light, which universally illumines the worlds of the ten directions, makes offerings to all Tathāgatas, and destroys the ground of ignorance (*avidyāvāsabhūmi*) of all sentient beings, causing them to attain the purity of the five eyes of a Tathāgata.

This light returns and merges back into one body; then, in order to allow all Bodhisattvas to enjoy the samādhi-wisdom, it takes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajra Lamp-Light Maidservant and dwells in the northwest corner of the Vajra Jewel Pavilion.

Vairocana Buddha realizes within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the ocean-like clouds of vajra unguent. For his own enjoyment, from this samādhi-wisdom of the ocean-like clouds of vajra unguent, he emits vajra-unguent light that illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, making offerings to all Tathāgatas and destroying all transgressions of improper conduct regarding the body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings, whereby they attain the fivefold uncontaminated *dharmakāya*.

This light returns and merges into one with him; then, in order to provide enjoyment for all Bodhisattvas through samādhi-wisdom, he takes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajra-Unguent Maidservant and dwells in the northeastern corner of the Vajra Jewel Pavilion.

The Buddha Vairocana, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the Hook for Summoning (Ākarṣaṇavajrāṅkuśa) for his own enjoyment, radiates light from the Hook for Summoning samādhi-wisdom in the form of vajra-hooks. This light pervades the worlds of the ten directions, summoning all Tathāgatas to the Vajradhātu maṇḍala and delivering all sentient beings from the evil realms, establishing them in the city of non-abiding nirvāṇa;
it then returns and merges back into a single essence.

In order to cause all bodhisattvas to enjoy the wisdom of samādhi, he manifests in the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa, the Guardian of the Door of the Bodhicitta, and dwells upon the moon disc at the eastern gate.

Vairocana Buddha, having internally realized the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Entrance-Means-Noose (*vajrāveśopāyapāśa-samādhi-jñāna*), for the sake of his own enjoyment, emanates from that samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra-Entrance-Means-Noose rays of light in the form of a vajra-noose. These illuminate the worlds of the ten directions, drawing in the assemblies of all Tathāgatas and binding all sentient beings who have sunk into the mire of the samādhi-wisdom of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the two vehicles. He establishes them within the palace of the Dharma-realm of the King of Awakening;

then, returning and reabsorbing [the light] into a single essence, for the sake of allowing all Bodhisattvas to enjoy this samādhi-wisdom, he manifests in the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāśa, the Guardian of the Merit-Gate, and dwells upon the moon-disc at the southern gate.

Vairocana Buddha, having realized within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Firm Vajra Shackles for his own enjoyment, radiates from that samādhi-wisdom of the Firm Vajra Shackles the light of the Vajra Shackles, which illuminates the worlds of the ten directions. This causes those who have already entered the Vajradhātu maṇḍala of the assembly of all Tathāgatas to be bound by the vow of great compassion and remain there; furthermore, it crushes the various views of non-Buddhists among all sentient beings, causing them to abide in the supreme city of enlightenment—firm, fearless, and non-retrogressive.

Returning to merge into one body, in order to provide the samādhi-wisdom for the enjoyment of all Bodhisattvas, he takes the form of the Bodhisattva Vajraśṛṅkhala, guards the gate of wisdom, and dwells upon the moon disc at the western gate.

Vairocana Buddha realized within his own mind the samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra Bell of Prajñāpāramitā; for his own enjoyment, he emitted from this samādhi-wisdom of the Vajra Bell of Prajñāpāramitā light-rays of the Vajra Bell that illuminated the worlds of the ten directions. This light gladdened the ocean-like assembly of all Tathāgatas dwelling in the Vajradhātu Maṇḍala and destroyed the dualistic views of the two vehicles of all sentient beings, establishing them in the palace of Prajñāpāramitā.

Returning and reabsorbing [the light] into his own body, in order to allow all Bodhisattvas to enjoy the samādhi-wisdom, he manifested in the form of the Vajraghaṇṭā Bodhisattva and dwelt upon the moon disc at the northern gate, guarding the entrance of diligence.
If explained according to sequential order, there would be a discrepancy between the preceding and the following;

however, based on the *saṃbhogakāya* Buddha, one suddenly realizes the three types of pure karma of body, speech, and mind, pervading the entire Dharma-realm. Within each and every dharma-gate, each and every principle, and each and every pore of the bodily marks and signs, they all exist throughout the realm of empty space without mutual obstruction, each remaining in its own place, thereby forming the self-enjoyment body and other-enjoyment body of the universally illuminating Vairocana.
If one speaks according to the sequence of the two vehicles, it is impossible to realize the fruit of the path without fully cultivating the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment.
To realize the Buddha-body of self-enjoyment, one must necessarily rely on the wisdom of thirty-seven samādhis to achieve the fruit of Buddhahood.
The *Gāthā-parivarta* of the Sanskrit *Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra* states:

"The nature-body (*svabhāva-kāya*), the enjoyment-body (*saṃbhoga-kāya*), the transformation-body (*nirmāṇa-kāya*), and the body of equal outflow (*niṣyanda-kāya*)—these thirty-six Buddha-qualities are all identical to the nature-body; together with the dharma-realm body (*dharmadhātu-kāya*), they total thirty-seven."
"Initially, having generated the bodhicitta of the Unsurpassed Vehicle, through the empowerment of Buddha Akṣobhya, he realized the perfect bodhicitta.
By virtue of that realization, externally, he received the consecration of Ratnasaṃbhava in the sky and attained the rank of Dharma King of the three realms."
Through the empowerment of the Buddha Avalokiteśvararāja, the wheel of speech is able to expound immeasurable sūtra-dharmas.
Through the empowerment of the Buddha Amoghasiddhi, all activities for the sake of the buddha-deeds and the welfare of sentient beings are fully accomplished.
Through the empowerment of the Vajra-pāramitā, one realizes the Great Perfect Mirror-like Wisdom that is fully perfected, pervading the Dharma-realm and encompassing all of space.
Through the empowerment of the Ratna-pāramitā, one realizes the Wisdom of Equality toward the infinite world of sentient beings and the infinite container-world.
Through the empowerment of the dharma-pāramitā, one attains the wisdom of wondrous observation regarding immeasurable gates of samādhi and dhāraṇī, as well as all dharmas of liberation.
Through the empowerment of the karma-pāramitā, one realizes the wisdom of accomplishing what is to be done regarding the establishment of immeasurable defiled worlds and pure worlds.
By the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva, one instantaneously realizes unsurpassed enlightenment through a sharp and intense mind.
By the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrarāja, one is endowed with the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) within the gateway of bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
By the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrarāga, he possesses a great compassion toward infinite sentient beings that is free from conditions and has never been interrupted.
By the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrasādhu, he thirsts for all wholesome dharmas without weariness, and upon seeing even the slightest bit of goodness, he praises it.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajraratna, one realizes undefiled wisdom, vast and perfect like space.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajraprabha, one attains the light of wisdom, which, like the solar disc, illuminates all without exception.

Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, he is able to fulfill all the worldly and transworldly aspirations of sentient beings; like a cintāmaṇi jewel banner, he satisfies them all without any conceptual discrimination in his mind.

Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrahasa, all sentient beings who see or hear him experience a surge of joy in their hearts; they become certain regarding the Dharma and receive its beneficial bliss.

Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajradharma, one realizes that the intrinsic nature of phenomena is pure and is able to expound all subtle and wondrous Dharma gates, knowing that all phenomena are like the parable of a raft.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajratīkṣṇa, one is able to sever the immeasurable afflictions, fetters, and sufferings of both oneself and others with the sword of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajra Cause, he requests all Tathāgatas throughout immeasurable Buddha-worlds to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajra Speech, the sixty-four kinds of Dharma-sounds pervade the ten directions, benefiting all sentient beings according to their respective types.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrakarma, one performs the great ritual of offering within the ocean-like assemblies of infinite Buddha-fields.

Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrarakṣa, one dons the armor adorned with great vows, returns to the cycle of birth and death to extensively act as a bodhisattva, and guides and nurtures sentient beings, establishing them in the Buddha-dharma.
By the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrayakṣa, one is able to destroy all Māras and externalists, and to weaken the enemies of beginningless afflictions.
By the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi, the immeasurable mantras, samādhis, and mudrās of the three secret gates are unified into a single essence.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajralāsyā, one attains mastery over the wisdom of enjoyment and experiences the perfect bliss of utilizing the Dharma.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajramālā, one obtains the flower garlands of the factors of enlightenment (bodhipakṣa-dharma) as adornment.

Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajragīta, one attains the subtle and wondrous voice of the Tathāgata, which those who hear never tire of; regarding the liberation of noble virtue, one realizes that all phenomena are like an echo.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajranṛtya, one attains the power to manifest emanated bodies with instantaneous swiftness, reaching limitless worlds in a single moment.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrajvālāgandha, one attains the fragrance of the Tathāgata’s pleasing and unimpeded wisdom.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrapuṣpa, one is able to open the wondrous flower of awakened mind within the mire of sentient beings' afflictions.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrapradīpa, one attains the purity of the five eyes, achieving mastery in illuminating the Dharma for the benefit of both self and others.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajragandha, one attains the five kinds of stainless, pure bodies of a Buddha.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa, one attains the samādhi of swiftly summoning all the noble assemblies.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāśa, one attains the skillful wisdom that is unimpeded like space.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrasphoṭa, one attains the liberation of the Buddha’s firm, untainted observation and great compassion.
Through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajraghaṇṭā, one attains the sound of the Tathāgata’s Prajñāpāramitā, by hearing which all evil seeds within the ālayavijñāna are destroyed.

By means of the empowerment of the wisdom-power of these thirty-seven internal realizations of the unsurpassed Vajradhātu, one suddenly realizes the body of Vairocana; from his invisible crown-mark (uṣṇīṣa), immeasurable *uṣṇīṣa*-dharmakāyas flow forth, gathering like clouds in the sky to form the dharma assembly.

Its light pervades everywhere like the parasol-rings of a stūpa; though those who have fulfilled the ten stages cannot behold it, it secretly bestows grace upon sentient beings, causing all karmic obstacles of body and mind to be utterly extinguished.
None can know it; yet even if they do not perceive it, it can still quell all sufferings and cause them to be reborn in auspicious realms.

From the light, sixteen bodhisattvas and the great protectors of the eight directions and other realms—both internal and external—emanate in succession, emitting rays that illuminate and touch the evil destinies. These form the tiers of a stūpa, guarding the stūpas and the palaces of the dharmadhātu of all Buddhas, and becoming the parasol-fillets (*cchattra-āvarta*). This causes one’s own body to manifest as the body of Vairocana, the All-Illuminating Tathāgata of the Vajradhātu.
